summary: Patch rewrites SSTable.delete() in SSTable.java to sort components by last-modified time and delete oldest first, replacing the DATA-first and SUMMARY-last ordering. Checklists applied: absence.md (registration, error-handling, sibling-path and rollback items) and completeness.md (callers, error mapping, refactor aftermath). Not reviewed: nothing; tier small, whole diff read. Findings: the tidier path in LogTransaction still deletes DATA first before calling SSTable.delete, so the ticket's scenario is not fixed there. The new loop also drops the confirmed-delete error path, so a failed component delete is now silent.

findings.rule: completeness: sibling/counterpart path for changed deletion order (ticket step 3, SSTableTidier)
findings.problem: The ticket's failing scenario is the SSTableTidier running after compaction. In LogTransaction.Tidier.run() the DATA file is still deleted first, unconditionally, via delete(datafile) at lines 390-396, before SSTable.delete(desc, ...) is called at line 401. The new timestamp sort in SSTable.delete only orders the remaining components. So after a crash mid-tidier, the DATA file is gone while newer components remain. On restart LogFile.verifyRecord() sees a changed latest update time for the REMOVE record and refuses to start the node, which is the bug the ticket describes. The fix is not applied on the path that actually produces the REMOVE records.
findings.fix: Remove the explicit DATA-first delete(datafile) in the tidier, keeping the datafile.exists()/!wasNew logging, and let SSTable.delete() order all components by last-modified time (including DATA). If the DATA-specific failure retry must be kept, perform the timestamp-ordered deletion in one place and keep the exception-to-retry behaviour.

findings.rule: absence: error handling symmetric with the original path; completeness: API contract (exceptions relied on by callers)
findings.problem: The original code deleted DATA and every non-SUMMARY component with FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(), which throws FSWriteError on failure. The new loop calls FileUtils.delete(String) for every component, and that method (FileUtils.java:545-552) discards the result of File.delete() and never throws. LogTransaction's tidier relies on an exception from SSTable.delete() to put the task on failedDeletions and retry (LogTransaction.java:401-406). Trigger: any component deletion fails (EACCES, EIO, a file locked on Windows). The new code returns normally, the tidier treats the sstable as fully deleted, the transaction log is cleared, and the remaining component files leak with no retry.
findings.fix: Restore the confirmed delete for the sorted components: call FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) in the loop, and keep the SUMMARY exception only if it was intentionally tolerant before (the original used FileUtils.delete there).
